text:
Love sits on the skull

Of Humanity,

And on such a throne the profane one,

With lewd laughter,


Cheerfully blows round bubbles,

Which rise in the air,

As if to join the worlds

At the depths of Ether.


The luminous and fragile globe,

In a wide flight,

Bursts and spits out its little soul

Like a golden dream.


And I hear the skull, at each bubble,

Pray and moan:

"This fierce and ridiculous fire,

When will it end?


For what your cruel mouth

Scatters in the air,

Murderous monster, is my brain,

My blood and my flesh!"

translation.title: Love and the Skull
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the grotesque allegory of Love blowing bubbles from humanity's skull.
